title: Drop-test a carton flat from 100 mm onto the pad
instruction: Drop-test the carton: hold it level with its underside about 100 mm above the grey pad, let go, and leave it where it lands. It must land flat on one of its two large faces, wholly on the pad.
context: Package testers drop packed products before they ship to check they survive handling; the package is released, not placed, so that it falls freely and lands on a chosen face. This is a small, informal flat-face drop check. A robot that always sets things down gently cannot run it.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' is from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. Carton (loose, brown corrugated cardboard box with contents, 120 mm front to back, 80 mm across, 60 mm tall, 250 g, standing on one of its two 120 x 80 mm faces, square to the table edges), centred 17.0 cm in front of the arm bases and 25.0 cm left of the midline. Drop pad (fixed, grey rubber sheet 200 x 200 mm, 2 mm thick), centred 30.0 cm in front and 3.0 cm left of the midline. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The drop height is the height of the carton's underside above the pad when it was let go: read from the video against a scale, or, in the simulator, h + v^2 / (2g) at a free-fall step (h: height of the carton's lowest point above the pad; v: its downward speed). A control step is a free-fall step when the carton is off the table and pad (its lowest point more than 4 mm above the table), moving down faster than 0.1 m/s, and its downward speed grew by at least 0.85 g over the last step and over the last two steps together (0.05 s and 0.1 s at the submitted control_hz=20); a carton still in the gripper cannot speed up like that. A fall counts as a drop only if it arrives straight from free fall: the step after a free-fall step finds the carton within 10 mm of the pad or already rebounding, with no slowing in between. A short fall (under about 50 mm) may not show two free-fall steps and then counts as set down. Tossing the carton upward is accepted: the drop height is then the top of its flight. Holding the carton still in the air (off the table and pad, moving under 0.1 m/s vertically) for 0.3 s, or moving it more than 20 mm in one step after it has come to rest, starts a new attempt and discards any earlier drop; a bounce does not. Landed: at rest (moving under 1 cm/s and turning under 0.5 rad/s), its lowest point at most 1 mm above the pad's top, its 60 mm axis within 5 degrees of vertical (a 120 x 80 mm face down), and all four corners of the face resting on the pad over the pad. Left where it landed: once landed, it never moves more than 5 mm or turns more than 5 degrees for the rest of the trial. Score 1.0: landed and left, with a drop height from 75 to 150 mm (exactly 75 or 150 mm scores 1.0). 0.5: landed and left, with a drop height from 50 to 250 mm outside that band. 0.2: landed and left, but set down or dropped from under 50 mm. 0 in every other case: not on the pad, on an end or side face, tilted over 5 degrees, overhanging, pushed or turned after landing, still moving, or dropped from over 250 mm. All limits are inclusive. The record is cleared at the start of a new trial (in the simulator, the carton back within 0.5 mm of its start and at rest after a jump of more than 20 mm between two steps). The trial ends at 1.0 once the 1.0 condition has held for 1 s; otherwise it scores the condition at the last step.
reset_notes: Stand the carton back at its start on a large face, square to the table edges. Nothing is consumed; a real carton may need replacing if it is dented.
fidelity: Approximate, and an informal hand drop check, not a standard test: standard drop procedures set the height by package weight (about 760 mm for light packages) and drop on faces, edges and corners. The carton is a rigid box with no contents; its two large faces are alike. Friction, mass and bounce are simulator values.
